text: The Trinity Bellwoods neighbourhood is a unique one in the City of Toronto and continues to change with more people living in less space in the downtown core. The need to ensure that our green spaces function to meet the needs of our residents is magnified when there is limited space to share and enjoy. Since 2016, my office has been working closely with local residents to determine their priorities for their neighbourhood park via community meetings and public surveys. The support for an enclosed dog off-leash area (DOLA) in Osler Playground, in addition to playground and aesthetic improvements is overwhelming. While the proposed enclosed DOLA does not quite meet the People, Dogs and Parks – Off-Leash Policy, it is important to note that many of the requirements listed in this policy are difficult to be met due to the unique character of the neighbourhood this DOLA would be located…

City Council on March 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council direct the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to work in consultation with the local Councillor toward the construction of a dog off-leash area in Osler Playground, in combination with a planning exercise for general park improvements.
